column2: I am still alive.{r}{p}Perhaps I should thank God for that.
In 1994, when 'Kamaitachi no Yoru' was released as software for the Super Famicom, I, its original author, succeeded in sneaking a secret document into a part of that cartridge
To stop a terrible conspiracy.
Read the secret document from back then?{@}
Read
Don't read
...This is the secret document from four years ago.
Let's get back to the matter at hand.
As was to be expected, within days of its release my act was discovered by “them,” and I was subjected to all kinds of torment in the torture room inside the company.
But the message surely reached the hands of several hundred users, and I believe that some of them took action to stop the conspiracy.
However, it seems Chunsoft's ambitions have not yet been extinguished.
This time they are re-releasing 'Kamaitachi no Yoru' as software for the PlayStation.
As a result, I was dragged out of my underground cell for the first time in four years and forced to help with the port.
Naturally, I can no longer use the “reset” part where I hid my accusing document before.
I had no choice but to pretend to touch up the text while making a new hiding place.
How many users will actually make it here?
And how many of them will stand up?
...If this is discovered, this time I will surely be killed.
All that's left is to entrust it to fate and pray.
That you, who are reading this now, survive and stop the conspiracy...
I don't know who you are, you who are reading this now.{r}{p}Whether child or adult, man or woman...{r}{p}Considering the people who buy this game
, a boy around high-school age is probably the most likely.
In any case, I desperately hope that you are an ordinary person who bought this software purely to enjoy a game, and not one of “them.”
I just wrote that I don't know who you are.{r}{p}But you should know who I am.{r}{p}At the very least you must have seen my name
on the game's package or in the staff roll.

My name is Takemaru Abiko.{r}{p}Or rather, I am the true author who hides in the shadow of the person known by that name.{r}{p}That is me.{r}{p}A photo of a face may appear on the package or in the manual
, but that is not me.{r}{p}That is one of “them,” using my name.
I was made to write nearly the entire story of this 'Kamaitachi no Yoru' in a room inside Chunsoft's offices.{r}{p}And right now I am writing this while pretending to work
and stealing past the eyes of “them.”{r}{p}Yes, “they” are none other than the employees of Chunsoft.
To be honest, at first I too was one of “them,” a Chunsoft employee.{r}{p}But as I took part in making this 'Kamaitachi no Yoru' and the project progressed
, I came to realize the true face of this company and its terrifying conspiracy.
Of course I tried to escape, but one step from freedom I was seized by “them.”{r}{p}Ever since, I have been confined in this room and forced to work
.{r}{p}Conveniently for “them,” I have no family and few friends outside the company, so probably no one will come looking for me.
The moment this job is finished, I will be killed.{r}{p}So most likely, by the time you are reading this, I have already been eliminated by “them”
.{r}{p}I tried many times to escape from here, but each time I was caught and subjected to countless tortures too dreadful to recall.

I no longer hold any hope of surviving, but I am writing this so the world will learn of their conspiracy and stop it.{r}{p}Behind an ordinary game, I hide this message so that it can only be found by solving a cipher
... I reasoned that this way I could pass information to people outside without “them” seeing it.
It would be ideal if I could plant this message in the master ROM, but in my position that is impossible.{r}{p}The most I can do is swap out one case, or two
Whether anyone among those few dozen copies will reach this message, and even if they read it, whether anyone will believe it... I have no idea at all
.{r}{p}And there is no guarantee that it won't be checked before shipping and destroyed by “them.”
...Let me stop worrying about this and that.{r}{p}Trusting that some good person is reading this, I will keep on writing.
You have probably heard the term subliminal perception somewhere.{r}{p}A stimulus too weak to notice... also called latent perception
.{r}{p}A sound too quiet to hear, an image shown for too short a time to recognize... such imperceptible stimuli influence the subconscious.
“They” tried to experiment with this subliminal perception in game software.{r}{p}The first was a game called 'Otogirisou.'
The embedded message was relatively harmless.{r}{p}“Chunsoft games are fun.”

The plan was to ship copies with the message embedded and copies without it to different regions, then compare sales of the next title to see the result.{r}{p}And the effect of the experiment was confirmed with a game called 'Torneko's Great Adventure'
.{r}{p}Sales in the regions where the message-embedded copies were shipped were remarkable.

Even at this stage you can see there is a certain commercial-ethics problem, but “their” true aim was not something as modest as business success.{r}{p}It was to brainwash the young people who will one day carry Japan on their shoulders while they are still children
and make them fanatical supporters of Chunsoft.

By the time the children who played this game grow up, Chunsoft will no longer be a mere game software company but a complex of religious organization, political association and multinational corporation
By then the brainwashed young people will worship Koichi Nakamura as a god, vote for the “Chunsoft Party,” and keep playing Chunsoft games like hollow wrecks while eating Chun Foods instant food
That is “their” goal.{r}{p}To rule all of Japan in economy, politics and faith.{r}{p}I know it sounds like a joke
.{r}{p}But it is the truth.
In fact, you, who must already have played this game several times, surely feel a strange sense of trust toward Chunsoft.{r}{p}If it's ten times or fewer, you are not yet fully brainwashed
.{r}{p}If you are reading this on your twentieth or thirtieth play, you probably won't believe anything I say.
But this is the truth.{r}{p}I want someone to expose “their” conspiracy.{r}{p}It's easy.{r}{p}All you have to do is make one phone call to the number I'm about to give you
.{r}{p}It is the number of the one friend I trust completely.{r}{p}Tell him everything.{r}{p}That's all.
There is no danger whatsoever.{r}{p}On the contrary, telling him will lower your risk.
...I considered keeping quiet so as not to frighten you, but it seems I can't.{r}{p}Even if I manage to sneak this message into a few dozen copies and mix them in with normal cartridges
, “they” will eventually notice that the count doesn't add up.
Once that happens, it is easy for “them” to trace the software to the retail stores.{r}{p}If you reserved your copy or bought it at a small shop, “they” will find you right away
.{r}{p}Even if you bought it at a large chain without reserving, you can't relax.

One month after release... that is probably all “they” need, with their power, to track down every copy.{r}{p}If you bought it more than a month ago, you are certainly under “their” surveillance right now
.{r}{p}High-performance directional microphones, infrared cameras... surely such things are aimed at you from just outside your room.
Wait!{r}{p}Don't even think of peeking outside the window.{r}{p}You'd make a perfect target for a rifle.{r}{p}Don't stand by the window.{r}{p}What you should do now
is crawl across the floor to the phone and call my friend.
“They” are right outside, deliberating whether to silence the one who found this message.{r}{p}There's no time.{r}{p}If you call and tell him everything
, killing you will be too late.{r}{p}So in order to survive, you must make that call.
Hurry.{r}{p}If you don't hurry, “they” will come.{r}{p}Pretending to collect for the newspaper.{r}{p}Or posing as electricians.{r}{p}...Ah, I hear “their” footsteps outside
